item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is substantially closer to the frozen contract because it adds the required replayable convenience API without changing global request handling or the existing Add behavior. Both patches improperly duplicate Add instead of routing through it, but A additionally introduces an explicitly prohibited retry-layer refactor with broad behavioral impact.","reasons":["B uses internal/multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", preserves the required Upload signature, validates inputs before a request, and returns helper read errors.","B keeps Add and unrelated retry machinery unchanged, matching the contract’s scope constraints.","A changes RawClient.Do to buffer nearly every non-native io.Reader whenever retries are not disabled. This affects all SDK requests, including Files.Update, despite the contract explicitly forbidding unrelated request/retry refactoring and requiring Add behavior to remain unchanged.","Both implementations duplicate Add’s option handling, request construction, decoding, and missing-data error instead of calling s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), violating an explicit reuse requirement. This is a smaller, localized correction in B than in A’s broader patch."],"risks_a":["The global buffering change can unexpectedly consume large or one-shot streaming bodies before any request and changes when source-reader errors occur across the SDK.","Conditioning buffering on isNoRetry(ctx) rather than whether retries are actually possible may add memory cost even when the configured policy will not retry the method.","Upload still bypasses Add, so the duplicated paths can drift despite A’s additional retry machinery and tests."],"risks_b":["Upload duplicates Add rather than delegating to it, leaving option, response, and error semantics vulnerable to future drift.","The retry test counts attempts but does not read and compare the multipart body on both attempts, so it weakly verifies the streamed-content replay requirement.","Validation combines empty-filename and nil-content failures into one error and the patch adds no explicit validation or source-reader-error tests, reducing diagnostic precision and contract verification."]}
